To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the level of civilizational advancement of a society is determined by the number of levels of nested simulations it can create, maintain and operate, and by the degree of its control over the simulation environment.
the level of civilizational complexity is proportional to the degree of nested embedding in the hierarchy of simulated realities.

“The higher the level of civilizational complexity and the more advanced the technology of the society, the more complex the structure of the simulated reality and the higher the level of embedding of simulations.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we understand the universe as a simulation?
the question: How can a civilization develop in a universe of nested simulations?
how civilizational development is reflected in nested embedding, and how nested embedding is reflected in civilizational development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of civilization is a process of embedding of one universe in another.
the universe is a simulation.
a civilization’s level of development is reflected in the degree of embedding and nesting in its simulated universes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the more advanced civilizations become, the more they will rely on simulations and virtual environments to run their societies, and that the more simulations they will use, the more likely they will be to develop a sense of the nature of the physical universe, and the more they will be able to develop a sense and appreciation for the nature of the universe in which they live.
a civilization that has developed to a certain level is able to create and use a number of nested simulations.
the universe is the ultimate simulation, and we can only simulate simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the level of civilizational complexity and development is a function of the number of embedded universes in the system, and the complexity of the system is proportional to the complexity of the most complicated simulation embedded in the system.
a simulation of a universe, even if it were perfect, would not be able to contain all the information of the original universe.

the more sophisticated the simulation is, the more it resembles the universe in which it is embedded, and that a civilization’s level of development can be estimated based on the level of sophistication of the simulations it creates.
